1997. Stack Operations Simulator

60

Medium

Problem Statement

Simulate a series of stack operations — PUSH, POP, and PEEK — and print the appropriate output for each.

Description

Read an integer q, the number of operations, followed by q operations. Each operation is one of: "PUSH x" (push the integer x onto the stack), "POP" (remove and print the top element, or print "Stack is empty" if the stack has no elements), or "PEEK" (print the top element without removing it, or print "Stack is empty" if the stack has no elements).
input_spec: The first line contains an integer q (1 ≤ q ≤ 100). Each of the next q lines contains one operation: either "PUSH x", "POP", or "PEEK".
output_spec:
for each.

Description

Read an integer q, the number of operations, followed by q operations. Each operation is one of: "PUSH x" (push the integer x onto the stack), "POP" (remove and print the top element, or print "Stack is empty" if the stack has no elements), or "PEEK" (print the top element without removing it, or print "Stack is empty" if the stack has no elements).

Input Description

The first line contains an integer q (1 ≤ q ≤ 100). Each of the next q lines contains one operation: either "PUSH x", "POP", or "PEEK".

Output Description

For every POP or PEEK operation, print the result on its own line. PUSH operations do not produce any output.
